decision: Can a person with an allergy distinguish declared absence, declared presence or trace, and missing data without CC implying safety?
liveConsumer: Food category and product decision surfaces that display allergen information.

gates.evidence: On 2026-07-15 the founder explicitly directed Codex to begin Phase 1. This capsule is limited to the S3 data-safety contract and does not claim app release readiness.
The founder's 2026-07-15 instruction to begin 1/X authorizes this bounded Phase 1 implementation in the isolated content worktree.

sourceRequirements: Authoritative EU-14 allergen definitions and labeling semantics.
The raw Open Food Facts allergen and trace fields actually consumed by the pipeline.
A measured baseline of mapped, unmapped, trace-only, and missing-data products.
An explicit three-state output contract that never converts missing data into declared absence.

preconditions.evidence: Read-only baseline frozen on 2026-07-15: 20,651 raw rows, 13,789 with allergen/trace tags, 6,862 without structured tags; 19,772 built products, including 4,736 unsafe declared-empty rows under the old contract.

The data transition preserves the legacy allergens union for filtering, adds distinct contains/trace/free fields, and makes declared true only when mapped structured evidence exists. App-owned per-allergen rendering will be logged as a release-blocking handoff.

doneWhen: EU-14 mappings and raw tag normalization are explicit and tested.
Declared, trace-only, and missing-data states cannot collapse into one another.
A build-failing audit catches unsafe state regressions.
The normal sequential rebuild finishes green.
The result card states coverage and limitations without making medical claims.
stopConditions: The gate remains blocked or write authorization remains false.
Raw source semantics cannot distinguish a required state.
The implementation would require an unapproved app-side semantic change.
Any audit suggests that missing data could be rendered as allergy-safe.
expectedArtifacts: A result card and append-only ledger entry.

claimBoundary.supports: CC can represent the covered source's allergen declarations and missingness without inferring safety.
claimBoundary.doesNotSupport: Medical advice, absence of cross-contamination, universal label completeness, or safety for any individual.
